clue.text: Lawyer (briefly) to question, with time, dubiously rebuked

indicators.note: briefly tells the solver to use the short written form of the legal title rather than the full word

parts.note: Att. is the standard abbreviation for Attorney
to question someone is to put a query to them
T is the usual abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A lawyer interrogates someone, and after some time the person is left feeling unfairly told off.
explanation.walkthrough: ATTASKT is a Spenserian word whose meaning is uncertain, often glossed as 'taken to task'; 'dubiously' admits that doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser's obscure form is usually taken to mean reproached or scolded, though dictionaries mark that sense as doubtful.

clue.text: A dozen Scotch cakes, say, consumed in west Wales

indicators.note: food consumed in something is taken inside it, so the answer lies within the following words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A dozen Scottish cakes are eaten somewhere in west Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: TWAL is the Scots form of twelve; 'cakes, say' just shows what might be counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Twal is the Scots word for twelve, so a Scot would count a dozen cakes this way.

clue.text: Major strike, event involving US eccentric

indicators.note: to involve something is to enfold it within, so one word is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a thing is an event or happening
wack is American slang for an eccentric or crazy person

explanation.surface: An industrial action is a big event, with an American oddball at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major strike' suggests industrial action, but it means a heavy blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A thwacking is a sound beating with heavy blows, so a strike of great force.

clue.text: Like indulged child, so plied with treating

definitions.text: Like indulged child, so plied with treating

indicators.note: treating something is processing it, so the preceding letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pampered child, plied with sweets and treats, is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as building it: a child plied with treats is just that.
explanation.definitionFit: An indulged child is ruined by too much pampering, described as overindulged in character.

clue.text: King having advantage with outstanding corporation

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: A king holds the advantage thanks to a prominent company behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is a jocular word for a paunch, and 'outstanding' means sticking out, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedge is a dialect adjective for pot-bellied, so someone whose big stomach protrudes.

clue.text: Med port, depressed about end of affluence

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mood word goes around the single letter

parts.note: triste is a literary word for sad or depressed

indicators.note: end of picks only the final letter of the next word

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean harbour town is gloomy now that its prosperity has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: The Med is the Mediterranean; Trieste is the Italian port on the Adriatic arm of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a major Italian seaport at the head of the Adriatic, part of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: What may be seen after stunning celebrities?

definitions.text: What may be seen after stunning
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the twinkling lights a dazed person sees after a blow to the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'stunning celebrities' reads as gorgeous famous people, but 'stunning' belongs to the first definition, meaning knocking out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone knocked dizzy is said to see twinkling lights, and famous performers are called by the same word.

clue.text: Old bird served by US restaurateur in his salad?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old name for a gull, especially the great black-backed gull

definitions.text: served by US restaurateur in his salad?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Bob ..., the Hollywood restaurateur who gave his name to a chopped chicken salad

explanation.surface: A tough old chicken ends up served in an American restaurant owner's signature salad.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cobb salad, which includes chicken, is named after Bob Cobb of the Brown Derby restaurant; the question mark flags that the bird may not really be in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an archaic dialect name for a large seagull and the surname behind a famous American chopped salad.

clue.text: See ending of concerto and of grand opera, maybe

definitions.text: See ending of concerto and of grand opera, maybe

parts.note: the word is said exactly like the name of the third letter

indicators.note: ending of takes just the final letter of each word that follows

parts.note: its final letter
its final letter
its final letter

explanation.surface: A reader is invited to look at how a concerto or a grand opera finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a closing passage is what you see at the end of such works.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding section of a musical piece, the passage that rounds off a movement or opera.

clue.text: What includes British flier I'd seen flapping?

definitions.text: What includes British flier I'd seen flapping?

indicators.note: flapping is agitated movement, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher asks what category covers a native bird seen with wings beating.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: a British bird spotted in flight is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdlife is the collective population of birds in an area, which naturally takes in any native flying species.

clue.text: Somewhat deformed by being guided round mine? …

parts.note: the word by is spelt B and Y, so it is read as those letters joined by the word and

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the guiding word goes about the explosive one

parts.note: someone being guided is led
egg is old service slang for a mine or bomb

explanation.surface: A visitor taken on a tour of a pit comes out a little misshapen.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading 'by' as its spelling, B and Y. The ellipsis runs on to the next clue, whose answer is a mine shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: Having legs that curve outward at the knee is a mild physical deformity, the condition also called bow legs.

clue.text: … Passage therein shaped by act, fast push

indicators.note: something shaped is formed into a new form, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the mine tour, a tunnel is dug out with quick hard pushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'therein' points back to the mine in the previous clue, which is why the clue opens with an ellipsis.
explanation.definitionFit: An upcast shaft is the ventilation passage in a mine through which stale air rises out of the workings.

clue.text: Being abnormally tense, forward on board in a hoy, sick?

indicators.note: a passenger on board a vessel is inside it, so one word goes inside the others
something sick is in a disordered state, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written; a hoy is a small coasting vessel
pert means cheeky or forward in manner

explanation.surface: A cheeky passenger aboard a little boat is seasick and stiff with nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the three words is split, with the inserted piece sitting in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypertonia is the medical term for excessive muscle tone, a state of abnormal tension in the muscles.

clue.text: Ornamental shell, one attached to hand

indicators.note: attached to means fixed on beside something, so one piece follows directly after the other

parts.note: paw is informal for a hand
a means one

explanation.surface: A decorative shell held in someone's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The hand comes first in the answer even though 'one' is written first.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawa, or paua, is the New Zealand abalone, whose iridescent shell is widely used in jewellery and ornament.

clue.text: Trouble with sailors on deck

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors are causing a commotion on the deck of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like part of a ship but is the verb meaning to decorate, as in 'deck the halls'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to decorate or ornament it, the same as to beautify it with trimmings.

clue.text: Clubman Jock's chatter takes in one with general intelligence

indicators.note: to take something in is to absorb it inside, so the chatter wraps round the other letters

parts.note: claver is Scots for idle chatter; Jock is a Scot
I is the Roman numeral one
g is the psychologists' symbol for general intelligence

explanation.surface: A club member listens to a Scot's chatter about someone of all-round cleverness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubman' reads as a member of a club, but means a man carrying a club, or a keeper of keys, from Latin clavis and clava.
explanation.definitionFit: A claviger is literally a club-bearer (or key-bearer), so a man who carries a club, punning on a club's member.

clue.text: Jewish period that finds Yemeni catching nasty rash (9, two words)

indicators.note: catching means trapping something inside, so the person holds the jumbled letters

parts.note: an Adeni is a native of Aden, a city in Yemen

indicators.note: a nasty condition is a bad, disordered one, so the letters of the skin complaint are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man from Yemen comes down with a nasty rash during a Jewish season.
explanation.definitionFit: Adar Sheni, the second Adar, is the extra leap-year month in the Hebrew calendar, so a calendar period.

clue.text: Wordy address: one resounded amid clamour

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so these words go inside the noise word

parts.note: hue, as in hue and cry, is an outcry or clamour
a means one
a bell rang out, resounded

explanation.surface: A long speech echoes around a noisy hall full of shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a lengthy, forceful speech, a long-winded address that lectures its audience.

clue.text: Yells with bed's shaking in heavenly style

indicators.note: shaking jumbles things about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone shouts while the bed rocks, an ironic picture of heavenly bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in a blessed way is to act as if in heaven, so an adverb of divine favour fits a heavenly manner.

clue.text: Oriental tipple to quench — litre disposed of

indicators.note: something disposed of is thrown away, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to slake a thirst is to quench it
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: A Japanese drink to quench thirst, with the litre bottle thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Sake is Japanese rice wine, a drink of the Far East, which older crosswords call Oriental.

clue.text: Wild praises for deities worshipped by expat Greeks

definitions.note: plural, because the god fused two older deities

indicators.note: wild means unruly and uncontrolled, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Greek settlers abroad sing extravagant praises to their gods.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'deities' is fair because Serapis was a merging of Osiris and Apis, worshipped by the Greeks of Ptolemaic Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Serapis was a Graeco-Egyptian god created by the Ptolemies, combining Osiris and Apis for the Greek settlers in Egypt.

clue.text: Fortifying outwork? More than one of them could form salient

indicators.note: could form means might be made into a new shape, so the letters of the last word are reshaped
the plural is what is rearranged, so its plural ending must be dropped to reach the single form

parts.note: taken as written; a salient is also a projecting part of a fortification

explanation.surface: A military engineer notes that several outworks together could make a salient.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay works backwards: the plural of the answer is an anagram of salient, and a salient is itself a projecting fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenail, or tenaille, is a low outer rampart built in front of the main curtain wall of a fort.

clue.text: Entails moving towards one coast of Scotland?

indicators.note: moving letters means putting them in new positions, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A journey that involves heading for one of Scotland's shores.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: the Scots word just means eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastlin is a Scots adverb meaning eastward, so heading for the North Sea side of the country.

clue.text: Valve (obsolete) was trying, with nothing in it

indicators.note: in it means placed inside the preceding word, so the nothing sits within it

parts.note: tride is an obsolete spelling of tried, as in Spenser
O is nothing, zero

explanation.surface: An old valve was tiresome to use, having nothing inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: '(obsolete)' looks like it describes the valve, a nicely apt idea, but it marks the old spelling of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A triode is a thermionic valve with three electrodes, used in early radios and amplifiers.

clue.text: Brightly coloured fish, fathom deep in seaweed

indicators.note: something deep in a thing is buried inside it, so one letter goes within the other word

parts.note: ore is a dialect word for seaweed, as in oreweed
F is the abbreviation for fathom

explanation.surface: A vivid fish swims a fathom down among the seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe is the ide, a freshwater fish whose golden variety is a popular ornamental pond fish.

clue.text: Something like marram, grand cooked in sauce (9, two words)

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the following word

parts.note: sass is cheek, impudence, also called sauce

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grand dish cooked in sauce sounds like a recipe, though the ingredient is a coarse dune plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' means cheek here, not a liquid for cooking; marram is a grass planted to bind sand dunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand grass is any grass growing on sandy shores, of the same kind as marram, which stabilises dunes.

clue.text: Mock Spenserian stuff, opening of epic

parts.note: gear is stuff, belongings

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A parody of Spenser's style, the opening lines of an epic like The Faerie Queene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock Spenserian' reads as imitation Spenser, but it means Spenser's word for mock.
explanation.definitionFit: Geare is Spenser's spelling of jeer, a taunt or mockery, so his word for ridicule.

clue.text: Fine pottery piece of tiling captured in ballad

indicators.note: something captured in another thing is held inside it, so the letter goes within the song

parts.note: an aria is a song, loosely a ballad

indicators.note: a piece of a word is a fragment of it, here its first letter

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A fragment of a decorated tile is caught in a song about fine china.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of tiling' looks like a broken tile, apt with pottery, but takes only one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arita is Japanese porcelain from the town of Arita, the source of Imari ware, prized fine pottery.

clue.text: Veteran rowers fell short

indicators.note: falling short means stopping before the end, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: fell as an adjective means fierce or cruel

explanation.surface: An old rowing team failed to reach the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like the past of fall but is the adjective meaning savage; 'Veteran' marks an obsolete spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Crue is an obsolete spelling of crew, so an old-fashioned word for a boat's team of oarsmen.

clue.text: Gather in fragments round house for aardvark

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the broken word encloses the abbreviation
a thing in fragments is broken up, so its letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Pieces are gathered up around a house, as if building a home for an aardvark.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth hog is another name for the aardvark, a burrowing African mammal; aardvark itself means earth pig in Afrikaans.

clue.text: Cook removing stew from cooker, modern

indicators.note: removing takes letters away, so those of the dish are struck out of what follows

parts.note: a stove is a cooker
new means modern
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: A chef takes the casserole off a new kitchen range.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the four letters of the dish out of the two joined words leaves the answer; 'Cook' is the verb, to bake in an oven.
explanation.definitionFit: To oven something is to bake or cook it in an oven, a verb use recorded in Chambers.

clue.text: Where to spot group assembled, gripped by Pythagoras?

indicators.note: a thing gripped by something is held within it, so the answer sits inside the name

parts.note: the letters run consecutively inside the philosopher's name

explanation.surface: A question of where a crowd gathered in the time of the Greek mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek setting makes the definition apt: Pythagoras would have known the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the open public square of an ancient Greek city, where citizens met for assemblies and markets.

clue.text: As of old, willingly in bar polishing last off

indicators.note: to polish off is to finish or remove, so the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a lever is a bar used for prising

explanation.surface: Someone in a bar is happily polishing things off, in old-fashioned style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it is a metal bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Leve is an obsolete form of lief, an adverb meaning gladly or readily, as in 'I'd as lief'.

clue.text: What's yet to appear turning out in fruit

indicators.note: turning things over changes their order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something not yet visible is emerging in a piece of fruit, like a seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' reads as a phrase meaning resulting, but 'out' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Futurition is the state of being yet to come, future existence, so whatever is still to appear.

clue.text: Set dropping even bits out of the blue

indicators.note: dropping the even-numbered letters leaves only the odd ones, first, third and so on

parts.note: the odd-placed letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A television set loses signal and goes blank out of the blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the blue' reads as a stock phrase, but 'out of' merely links and only the last two words supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tele is informal for a television set, the box in the corner.

clue.text: Which chant suggests a degree of polish?

indicators.note: suggests here means the answer, read as a phrase of letters and a word, describes how to spell the chant

parts.note: a chant is to sing; that word is S followed by ING

explanation.surface: A choirmaster asks which chant shows the singers have some polish.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'S and ING': that phrase spells out SING, the chant. 'polish' means a smooth finish, not refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing wood with abrasive paper smooths it, a stage of polishing a surface to a fine finish.
